guardian.description:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

The virus causing a massive outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could be mutating, health officials fear, as confirmed cases pass 4,000.

Africa’s public health watchdog said the time for incremental action was over as they announced plans to scale up every aspect of the response and go “door to door” looking for patients.

State department informs Congress of planned closures in Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia and Cameroon

guardian.description:
Tropical cyclone brings torrential rain and high winds to east coast after hitting Japan’s southern Okinawa province

Typhoon Dolphin, the most powerful tropical cyclone to hit China this year, has made landfall on the country’s east coast, bringing torrential rain and strong ⁠winds and triggering warnings ​of flooding and landslides.

The storm has already swept through Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

guardian.description:
Imports this year now account for 14% of the market amid claims vehicles are being dumped in the EU and UK

Chinese electric car sales have risen across Europe to a record high driven by strong demand and low tariffs in the UK and a surge in buyers in Italy.

The death toll from a school shooting in Thailand rose to nine on Saturday, after police said a 12-year-old girl caught up in Friday’s incident had died.

Nintendo has reported a jump in profits, as the Japanese game maker’s earnings were buoyed up by a long-awaited refund on Donald Trump’s tariffs.

The company said profits surged 53.5% to ¥147.4bn (£694m) over the three months to June, substantially beating expert forecasts for ¥77.8bn.

rfi.title: Demi Vollering wins Women's Tour de France for the second time
rfi.description: Dutch cyclist Demi Vollering on Sunday won her second Women’s Tour de France title, dethroning defending champion Pauline Ferrand-Prévot from France, who dropped out of the race on Saturday. Vollering excelled during the hilly final stage to extend her lead on nearest rival Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney, who finished second overall.

rfi.title: Netanyahu rejects Gaza plan in new break from Trump
rfi.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday rejected a US-led Gaza plan endorsed by Hamas, putting distance between himself and President Donald Trump as he tries to shore up his base ahead of close elections.

rfi.title: As the planet heats up, butterflies are seeking out cooler climes
rfi.description: Climate change is driving shifts in where butterflies are found globally, according to a major new study, with some species moving northwards or seeking out higher elevations in search of cooler conditions.

rfi.title: Investigation raises alarm over uranium in DRC cobalt shipments to China
rfi.description: An investigation by Lighthouse Reports, The Financial Times and Le Monde traces the possible export of uranium from the Democratic Republic of Congo back to a confidential International Atomic Energy Agency memo obtained in 2024. Chinese mining group CMOC, which owns the main site examined in Katanga, disputes the findings.

rfi.title: Rise in injuries sees Paris police impose new rules on e-scooter users
rfi.description: Electric scooter riders in Paris must now wear helmets and reflective gear under new rules introduced after a significant rise in injuries involving the two-wheelers, police said at the weekend.

rfi.title: Sall's chances at UN secretary-general role weakened after first vote
rfi.description: Antonio Guterres’s successor as United Nations secretary-general will be named in October. So far, two candidates from the African continent – Senegal’s Macky Sall and Uganda’s Olara Otunnu – have failed to win sufficient support.

rfi.title: Morocco, Algeria reach WAFCON semi-finals and World Cup
rfi.description: A triumphant night for north Africa ended on Saturday with hosts Morocco and Algeria reaching the Women's Africa of Nations (WAFCON) semi-finals and the 2027 World Cup in Brazil.

rfi.title: WAFCON: Ghana set up last eight clash with Fazili's Malawian debutants
rfi.description: Ghana will take on tournament newcomers Malawi on Sunday for a place in the semi-finals at the 2026 women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) after a 1-1 draw with Mali.

rfi.title: Spain begins border checks on travellers from Italy amid migration showdown
rfi.description: Spain on Saturday began temporary border checks on travellers from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures at the end of July, after a mass migrant rush into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta.

rfi.title: Think this summer is hot? El Nino could push temperatures even higher
rfi.description: Record ocean heat, intensifying El Nino conditions and worsening extremes are raising the prospect that 2026 could become the hottest year ever measured.

rfi.title: French farmers bracing for smallest corn harvest in 40 years
rfi.description: France's corn harvest is on pace this year for a 35 percent fall to nine million tons, a level last seen in 1980 for Europe's biggest grains producer, the government said Friday.

rfi.title: Former French PM Attal files legal complaint over alleged Russian interference
rfi.description: Former French prime minitser Gabriel Attal, also a candidate in the 2027 presidential election, has filed a legal complaint alleging "foreign interference originating from Russian networks" after discovering he was the target of several deepfakes, fake news videos and fake newspaper front pages earlier this week.

rfi.title: High stakes for Ireland's EU presidency amid migration row over Ceuta crisis
rfi.description: Ireland this week found itself at the centre of Europe’s increasingly fraught migration debate, as it sought to calm a dispute among European Union member states following last week's influx of 50,000 people into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta.

rfi.title: Turkey's new opposition party offers hope, but its future is already in jeopardy
rfi.description: The launch of the Yeni Party in Turkey promises to energise the country's struggling opposition. But while some polls show it leading, it remains vulnerable – already beset by arrests it says are "politically motivated".

rfi.title: Ivorian drum, looted by France, goes on display for first time at home
rfi.description: The Djidji Ayokwe, a sacred "talking drum" which was looted by French colonial troops in 1916 and taken to France, arrived in its home village in Côte d'Ivoire on Friday, where local people were able to see it for the first time since it was repatriated in March.

rfi.title: The EU has new anti-Beijing instruments, but will China have to face the music?
rfi.description: When Western companies rushed into China in the 1980s and 1990s, they traded their latest technology for market access. Now, China has absorbed, adapted and improved foreign know-how and is flooding Europe with advanced products, while the European Union's trade deficit balloons. As Paris and Berlin finally align on a response, analysts question whether Brussels' defensive "instruments" can contain a rival it helped create.

rfi.title: Rwanda in talks with Italy to take in migrants trying to reach EU
rfi.description: Days after Italy proposed setting up a network of migrant reception centres outside the European Union, Rwanda has confirmed that it is in talks with the Italian government about potentially hosting people seeking asylum in the EU.

rfi.title: Pope Leo XIV to meet survivors of clerical abuse during September visit to France
rfi.description: Pope Leo XIV will meet privately with survivors of clerical sexual abuse during a four-day visit to France next month. On Friday, the Vatican published the itinerary for the 25–28 September trip – the first papal state visit to the country since Benedict XVI visited in 2008.

euronews.title: Don Nelson, the second-winnigest head coach in NBA history, dies aged 86
euronews.description: The legendary coach and former player, credited for introducing the “Nellie ball”, was inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame as a coach in 2012 for – at the time – holding the most wins as a head coach in NBA history.

euronews.title: 'Ceuta is Spain': Hundreds protest government over migration crisis
euronews.description: Hundreds of Ceuta residents gathered on Sunday to demand an “immediate, decisive and proportionate” response to the migration crisis. The protest, organised by the city’s four religious communities, was marked by criticism of the central government and calls for unity.

euronews.title: Messi says farewell to his father in hometown Rosario
euronews.description: Lionel Messi attended a private funeral for his father and longtime agent Jorge Messi at El Prado cemetery in Rosario on Sunday, days after his death at the age of 68.

euronews.title: Suspected Irish crime boss Daniel Kinahan extradited from Dubai to Dublin
euronews.description: Kinahan is believed to have run the Kinahan organised crime group, which is suspected of trafficking narcotics into Ireland, the UK and Spain, as well as a slew of other charges, including money laundering and murder.

euronews.title: Poland now sixth-largest EU economy, ahead of Switzerland and Belgium
euronews.description: Poland's economy is gaining in importance in Europe. In 2025 the country ranked sixth in the EU by nominal GDP, accounting for almost 5% of the bloc's total output.

euronews.description: The fires that erupted on Friday spread rapidly, nearly doubling in size overnight into Saturday. National police are investigating a possible death near Summerland, although the casualty has not yet been confirmed.

euronews.title: Over 1 million evacuated as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
euronews.description: Typhoon Dolphin made landfall in densely populated eastern China on Sunday, meteorological authorities said, after the storm triggered more than 1,000 flight cancellations, 1 million evacuations, and a top-level alert.

euronews.title: 13 killed in Ukraine and 90 injured as Russia intensifies overnight bombardment campaign of Ukrainian cities
euronews.description: 13 people were killed and some 90 others were wounded over the past 24 hours as Russian attacks as the Kremlin intensifies its bombardment of Ukrainian cities. Meanwhile, Moscow says five people were killed in Ukrainian drone attacks targeting Russian cities.

euronews.title: Israel 'rejects' the US ceasefire plan for Gaza accepted by Hamas
euronews.description: At a cabinet meeting, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the army would make 'no withdrawal until Hamas is truly disarmed,' scrapping the ceasefire plan.

euronews.title: Party in the dry Danube riverbed: many call it a natural disaster
euronews.description: Just as musicians kept playing on the Titanic while the ship went down, in Budapest, the exposed bed of the shrinking Danube River has become a party spot.

euronews.title: Fires in Huelva and Castellón force evacuation of hundreds of residents
euronews.description: Over 150 firefighters worked overnight to stabilise the Niebla blaze, west of Sevilla. The fire has burned 4,000 hectares and displaced nearly 400 people. Air crews reinforced the Tírig fire in Castellón, east coast of Spain, at daybreak.

euronews.title: Cypriot natural gas flowing to Europe in 2028, says Cyprus Energy Minister
euronews.description: In an exclusive interview with the Associated Press, he highlights the progress of Cyprus's ongoing energy projects, which will also benefit EU citizens.

euronews.title: Major oil find off Polish-German border: Warsaw seeks drilling, Germany objects
euronews.description: In 2025, a Canadian firm found a major oil and gas field off Poland’s Baltic coast, the biggest since WWII, sparking German fears for the environment and tourism.

euronews.title: 'We see raped girls', doctor reveals horrors faced by migrant girls following Ceuta influx crisis
euronews.description: At least four migrant girls under the age of 14 have been treated at Ceuta University Hospital after alleged sexual assaults following last week's influx of migrants into Spain's north African exclave.

euronews.title: Nagasaki 81st atomic bomb anniversary unnerves proponents of pacifism
euronews.description: Nagasaki marked on Sunday the 81st anniversary of the US atomic bombing of the southwestern city, as the mayor called nuclear weapons “absolute evil,” denounced growing support for nuclear deterrence, and called on the Japanese government to adhere to its three postwar non-nuclear principles.

euronews.title: Yemen's Houthis attack kills 11 in Yemen, hit Saudi refinery
euronews.description: Strikes by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Sunday killed at least 11 people in the Yemeni port city of Mokha, says a medical source, after an earlier drone salvo targeted a Saudi oil refinery. Attacks from the armed group have increased since the 2022 truce seems to have been broken last month.

lemonde.title: Clémence Girard, directrice de la section criminalité organisée du parquet de Paris : « L’Ile-de-France est une importante destination de stupéfiants »
lemonde.description: Témoin de l’évolution du narcobanditisme dans la région, Clémence Girard, directrice de la section criminalité organisée du parquet de Paris, revient, dans un entretien au « Monde », sur la montée en puissance des factions criminelles et leur organisation à partir du territoire francilien.

lemonde.title: Tour de France Femmes 2026 : Demi Vollering s’impose lors de la dernière étape à Nice et remporte la Grande Boucle pour la deuxième fois
lemonde.description: La Néerlandaise de 29 ans a remporté, dimanche, la 9ᵉ et dernière étape de la Grande Boucle 2026, après avoir distancé Katarzyna Niewiadoma. Elle décroche son deuxième succès dans l’épreuve après l’édition 2023.

lemonde.title: Trente ans après le meurtre du rappeur Tupac Shakur, un procès pour résoudre une affaire jamais élucidée
lemonde.description: Le procès de Duane « Keefe D » Davis, accusé d’avoir organisé et participé au meurtre, en 1996, du rappeur Tupac Shakur, débute lundi 10 août à Las Vegas. Personne n’a jamais été condamné dans cette affaire, l’un des plus célèbres « cold case » de l’histoire américaine.

lemonde.title: « Si vous voulez travailler, vous travaillez demain » : à Loudéac, l’indispensable main-d’œuvre des salariés roumains
lemonde.description: « Venu(e)s d’ailleurs » (4/7). Plusieurs milliers de Roumains sont venus travailler en Bretagne depuis l’entrée de leur pays dans l’Union européenne. Avec ses nombreux emplois, sa mission orthodoxe et son épicerie spécialisée, la petite ville des Côtes-d’Armor est un pôle d’attraction pour cette diaspora laborieuse.

lemonde.title: La guerre des serviettes : « Vous avez vu ce qui s’est passé en Catalogne ? »
lemonde.description: « Les douleurs des vacances » (4/7). Au bord de la piscine, le drap de bain posé sur un transat vide vaut titre de propriété. La course à la privatisation commence donc dès l’aube et peut parfois aller jusqu’au tribunal. Une situation alarmante pour les établissements touristiques.

lemonde.title: Violences sexuelles sur mineurs : la police judiciaire dénonce une « trahison » de Gérald Darmanin
lemonde.description: L’Association nationale de police judiciaire a réagi, dimanche, au courrier – révélé par « Le Monde » – adressé par le ministre de la justice à son homologue de l’intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, dévoilant les graves défaillances des services d’enquête dans la prise en compte des violences faites aux mineurs.

lemonde.title: Canicule et orages : vingt-deux départements seront en vigilance orange lundi
lemonde.description: Météo-France a en outre placé les départements de la Haute-Garonne, du Gers, des Landes, du Lot-et-Garonne, des Pyrénées-Atlantiques, des Hautes-Pyrénées, du Tarn et du Tarn-et-Garonne en vigilance orange pour des orages localement très violents, prévus dimanche en fin d’après-midi.

lemonde.title: Israël « rejette » le plan américain pour Gaza accepté par le Hamas, annonce Benyamin Nétanyahou
lemonde.description: L’Etat hébreu a rejeté le document présenté fin juillet par le Conseil de la paix de Donald Trump. Son armée « n’effectuera aucun retrait [du territoire palestinien] tant que le Hamas ne sera pas véritablement désarmé », a déclaré Benyamin Nétanyahou.

lemonde.title: L’incendie dans la Drôme s’est étendu, un total de 370 hectares brûlés et quatre pompiers blessés
lemonde.description: Parti lundi près de Bellegarde-en-Diois, dans le massif du Claps, le feu a connu deux reprises dans la matinée de dimanche. Un autre incendie, qui s’est déclaré dimanche midi en Lozère, avait déjà parcouru plus de 100 hectares en fin d’après-midi, selon les pompiers locaux.

lemonde.title: Après l’incendie en Gironde, le retour dans leurs Ehpad des seniors évacués en urgence
lemonde.description: Face aux incendies, 2 388 personnes vulnérables ont été évacuées des établissements de Gironde et des Landes. A l’Ehpad Paul-Louis-Weiller d’Arès, 16 résidents sont rentrés, vendredi 7 août. Une joie et un soulagement pour eux et pour les équipes.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : un drone de combat explose en Moldavie, près de la frontière entre les deux pays
lemonde.description: Une « puissante explosion », qui serait due à un drone de combat, a été signalée dans le village de Crocmaz, dans le sud-est de la Moldavie. Les fragments sont analysés par des spécialistes.

lemonde.title: Le typhon Dolphin a touché terre dans l’est de la Chine ; des fortes pluies et des vents violents sur de larges portions du littoral
lemonde.description: Le Centre météorologique national de Chine a émis dimanche matin une alerte rouge au typhon – son niveau le plus élevé – prévoyant des « pluies torrentielles exceptionnelles » dans certaines zones du centre et de l’est du Zhejiang.

lemonde.title: Du sage ascète à l’influenceur suivi par des millions de followers : comment l’Occident a refaçonné l’hindouisme... et vice-versa
lemonde.description: « Gourous et ashrams, la ruée vers l’Ouest » (6/6). L’attrait des Occidentaux pour les religions orientales n’est pas sans effet sur ces dernières, qui ressortent transformées de leurs échanges. De sorte que l’on ne sait plus bien si c’est l’Occident qui s’orientalise, ou l’Orient qui s’occidentalise.

lemonde.title: L’été contrarié de Léon Marchand, diminué par une blessure à l’approche des championnats d’Europe de natation à Paris
lemonde.description: Le Toulousain de 24 ans sera la tête d’affiche de la compétition continentale, qui débute lundi à Saint-Denis. Mais une blessure survenue en juin, puis une rechute ont freiné sa préparation, changé son programme et remis un temps en question sa participation.

lemonde.title: Maria Angelicoussis, la discrète armatrice la plus puissante de Grèce
lemonde.description: Le groupe Angelicoussis, qu’elle dirige depuis 2021, est le plus grand armateur privé du monde en tonnage, et profite de l’essor du gaz naturel liquéfié en Europe. La PDG de 44 ans est la femme la plus riche de Grèce.

france24fr.title: 🔴 La Néerlandaise Demi Vollering remporte le Tour de France femmes et s'offre un deuxième sacre
Tour de France femmes : la Néerlandaise Demi Vollering s'offre une deuxième Grande Boucle
france24fr.description: Après une victoire en 2023, la Néerlandaise Demi Vollering a remporté dimanche son deuxième Tour de France femmes, devançant la Polonaise Kasia Niewiadoma au classement général. Elle était arrivée en deuxième position en 2025.

france24fr.title: La Syrie annonce un accord sur le sort des bases russes situées sur la côte méditerranéenne
france24fr.description: Fruit d'un an et demi de négociations, un accord a été trouvé entre Damas et Moscou sur l'avenir de deux bases russes sur le territoire syrien, a annoncé le ministère syrien des Affaires étrangères, cité par Sana, dimanche. Les installations militaires du port de Tartous et de l'aéroport de Hmeimim, situées sur la côte méditerranéenne, seront transformées "en centres conjoints de formation".

france24fr.title: Vingt-deux départements placés en vigilance orange canicule lundi, selon Météo-France
france24fr.description: Météo-France a placé, dimanche, 22 départements du centre et du sud-est du pays en vigilance orange "canicule", dont neuf nouveaux par rapport à dimanche. Un nouvel épisode caniculaire pourrait "s'étendre à de nombreuses régions de France", estime un prévisionniste.

france24fr.title: Selon Volodymyr Zelensky, jusqu'à 50 000 soldats nord-coréens ont été déployés en Russie
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky estime entre 30 000 et 50 000 le nombre de soldats nord-coréens déployés pour combattre aux côtés de la Russie, alliée de Pyongyang. Face à ce partenariat, il a exhorté Séoul à renforcer sa coopération avec Kiev, et notamment pour des systèmes de défense aérienne.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : Tel Aviv "rejette" le plan américain accepté par le Hamas
france24fr.description: Noga Tarnopolsky, correspondant France 24, décrypte la situation.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : Téhéran pose ses conditions sur le détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: Bruno Daroux, chroniqueur international France 24, analyse la situation.

france24fr.title: Affaire des élèves disparus au Mexique : un ancien gouverneur arrêté
france24fr.description: Un ancien gouverneur accusé d'avoir dissimulé des preuves dans l'affaire des 43 étudiants disparus en 2014, qui a secoué le Mexique et reste non résolue, a été arrêté, a annoncé jeudi le bureau du procureur général. Les étudiants de l'école normale d'Ayotzinapa ont disparu le 26 septembre 2014 dans l'Etat de Guerrero (sud), alors qu'ils se rendaient en autocar à Mexico pour participer à une manifestation.

france24fr.title: Rebecca Enonchong, entrepreneuse camerounaise dans les hautes sphères du commerce mondial (1/3)
france24fr.description: Innovation africaine (1/3). Pionnière de la tech en Afrique, entrepreneuse aux multiples casquettes, Rebecca Enonchong a été nommée en juin vice-présidente de la Chambre de commerce internationale, une première pour une femme africaine. Portrait d'une "success woman" boulimique de travail, réputée pour ses prises de position tranchées tant dans le monde des  affaires qu'en politique.

france24fr.title: Incendies dans le monde, fusillade en Thaïlande, guerre au Moyen-Orient : la semaine en images
france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine et les images les plus spectaculaires : les incendies persistent en Europe et en Amérique, bien que la majorité des feux de forêt en France soient stabilisés, une fusillade est survenue dans une école en Thaïlande faisant plusieurs morts, et la guerre se poursuit au Moyen-Orient.

france24fr.title: Foot : la Fifa dénonce "un effort concerté et continu" pour affaiblir Infantino
france24fr.description: La Fédération internationale de football a dénoncé "un effort concerté et continu de certains pour affaiblir la Fifa et son président" Gianni Infantino, samedi dans un communiqué. "Des informations publiées récemment comportaient des affirmations non étayées et des allégations manifestement fausses concernant la Fifa et son président. france24fr.title: Etats-Unis : le cancer de Joe Biden s'est aggravé, son fils s'inquiète
france24fr.description: Le cancer dont est atteint l'ex-président américain Joe Biden s'est aggravé avec des métastases "dans ses os et au-delà", a indiqué son fils Hunter dans un entretien à la BBC, décrivant une maladie "très douloureuse" et "très invalidante".

france24fr.title: L'Espagne commence les contrôles aux frontières aux voyageurs venant d'Italie
france24fr.description: Selma Hadj-Bouziane est en direct de Madrid.

france24fr.title: Canicule sans fin à Antibes : 5ème vague de chaleur en France
france24fr.description: Douze départements du centre-est et du sud-est seront en vigilance orange canicule samedi et dimanche, selon le dernier bulletin de Météo-France, qui prévoit notamment des pics de chaleur dans le sud-ouest et le long de la vallée du Rhône.

france24fr.title: Téhéran pose ses conditions à toute réouverture du détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: Siavosh Ghazi est en direct de Téhéran.

france24fr.title: Colombie : deux attaques après l'élection du nouveau président
france24fr.description: Deux attaques, ayant tué un policier et fait plusieurs blessés, ont marqué samedi en Colombie le premier jour au pouvoir du nouveau président Abelardo de la Espriella, qui a promis des mesures radicales pour lutter contre le crime organisé. Cet ancien avocat représentant de la droite dure entame son mandat au moment où la Colombie traverse sa pire vague de violence depuis une décennie.

france24fr.title: Terrorisme masculiniste  : une trentaine d'hommes interpellés en France
france24fr.description: Une trentaine d'utilisateurs d'un canal Telegram masculiniste sont convoqués à partir de l'automne devant le tribunal de Paris pour répondre notamment de provocation à la haine envers les femmes. Les gendarmes ont interpellé en juin puis entendu 45 personnes, membres du canal Telegram public "femmeblancherie" (1.758 abonnés principalement francophones), a précisé le parquet.

france24fr.title: Contrôles aux frontières : bras de fer diplomatique entre Rome et Madrid
france24fr.description: L'Espagne a commencé samedi à effectuer des contrôles temporaires aux frontières, à ses ports et aéroports, pour les voyageurs en provenance d'Italie, première journée d'application de cette réponse aux mesures similaires imposées par Rome après l'afflux de migrants à Ceuta.

Verkehrsunfall: Fehler beim Abbiegen: Zwei Tote bei Unfall

zeit.description: Ihre größte Konkurrentin warf ihrem Team Unfairness vor, doch auf der letzten Touretappe fährt Demi Vollering allen davon. Und beweist wieder, wer die Beste der Welt ist.

Basketball: Nowitzkis erster NBA-Trainer: Don Nelson ist tot
Organisierte Kriminalität: Mutmaßlicher Gangster-Boss nach Irland ausgeflogen
Waldbrand in Südfrankreich: Neuer Waldbrand in Frankreich, Hunderte fliehen in Spanien vor Feuer
zeit.description: In Südfrankreich sind Hunderte Feuerwehrleute gegen Waldbrände im Einsatz. In Spanien gab es seit Jahresbeginn mehr als doppelt so viele Großbrände wie 2025.

zeit.title: Femosphere: Der weibliche Incel heißt Femcel
zeit.description: Manosphere: ist bekannt. Aber Femosphere? Unterwegs in einer Onlinewelt, in der Frauen über ihr Leben ohne Sex, Liebe, Intimität reden – und über den Hass auf Männer.

zeit.title: USA: US-Verteidigungsministerium fordert schnellere Waffenproduktion
zeit.description: Durch den Krieg gegen Iran schwinden die Waffenreserven der USA. Das Verteidigungsministerium fordert nun die Rüstungsindustrie auf, die Produktion zu beschleunigen.

zeit.title: Notfälle: Drei Verletzte durch Schüsse in Dänemark
Beach-Volleyball: Ehlers und Ersatzpartner Wüst: Nach Hamburg-Sieg EM-Favorit
Vermessung von Straftätern: Die Anatomie der Verbrecher
zeit.description: Im Paris des 19. Jahrhunderts begann die Vermessung von Straftätern. Ein Professor aus Sachsen setzt sie heute digital fort.

zeit.title: Tour de France Femmes: Niederländerin Demi Vollering gewinnt die Tour de France der Frauen
zeit.description: Bei der Tour de France Femmes war Demi Vollering nach einer Attacke 15 Kilometer vor dem Ziel nicht mehr einzuholen. Der dritte Tagessieg führt zu ihrem zweiten Titel.

zeit.title: Jemen: Huthis greifen Saudi-Arabien nach Abschluss von Verteidigungspakt an
zeit.description: Die Huthi-Miliz attackiert eine Ölanlage in Saudi-Arabien und einen Hafen im Jemen. Zuvor hatte Saudi-Arabien ein neues Bündnis mit Pakistan und der Türkei verkündet.

spiegel.title: Tupac Shakur: Mordprozess gegen mutmaßlichen Täter beginnt in Las Vegas
spiegel.description: Er war einer der einflussreichsten Hip-Hop-Stars der Neunzigerjahre – über Jahrzehnte blieb der Mord an Tupac Shakur ein Cold Case. Nun könnte ein Gerichtsverfahren den Fall zumindest teilweise aufklären.

spiegel.title: USA: Pentagon ruft Industrie auf, schneller Waffen zu produzieren
spiegel.description: Das US-Militär sieht sich immer häufiger mit leeren Arsenalen konfrontiert. Der Irankrieg verbrauchte Unmengen an Raketen und Munition. Jetzt greift das US-Kriegsministerium durch - und setzt sogar Fristen.

spiegel.title: Schweizer Demokratie: Schatten auf der Alpenrepublik
spiegel.description: Die Schweizer Demokratie wird oft als vorbildlich bezeichnet. Doch als die Weltkriege das Land auf die Probe stellten, warf die Eidgenossenschaft demokratische Werte schnell über Bord. Auch heute gilt Teilhabe nicht für alle.

spiegel.title: Die Linke in Sachsen-Anhalt: Warum Heidi Reichinnek ein Männer-Problem hat
spiegel.description: Linken-Frontfrau Heidi Reichinnek spricht vor allem junge Frauen in Städten an. Diese Strategie könnte ihrer Partei bei den Wahlen in Sachsen-Anhalt zum Verhängnis werden.

spiegel.title: Iran: Mohsen Resai übernimmt Vorsitz im Nationalen Sicherheitsrat
spiegel.description: Der ehemalige Kommandeur der Revolutionswächter Mohsen Resai leitet nun den Nationalen Sicherheitsrat in Iran. Der Einfluss der Wächter auf Irans Regierung könnte somit noch größer werden.

spiegel.title: »Die Odyssee« von Christopher Nolan: Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten
spiegel.description: In der Diskussion um Christopher Nolans Homer-Adaption werden alle plötzlich zu Altphilologen. Sie wollen leidenschaftlich mitreden? Die wichtigsten Antworten und Fakten vor oder nach Ihrem Kinobesuch.

spiegel.title: Strandbäder in Italien: Wie ein 23-jähriger Politiker sich für freie Strände einsetzt
spiegel.description: Italiens Strände gehören zu den schönsten der Welt und sind ein dickes Geschäft. An vielen haben selbst Italiener nur Zutritt, wenn sie zahlen. Ein junger Politiker macht mit Instagram-Videos dagegen mobil.

spiegel.title: Nepal: Leichen von deutschem Bergsteiger und vier Vermissten geborgen
spiegel.description: Im November vergangenen Jahres kamen sie durch eine Lawine in Nepal ums Leben. Nun konnten die Leichen von fünf Bergsteigern, darunter ein Deutscher, vom Unglücksort geholt werden.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Wie sich Tschernobyl gegen Russlands nächsten Invasionsversuch wappnet
spiegel.description: Zu Beginn der Invasion besetzten Putins Truppen die Atomruine nördlich von Kyjiw. Heute herrscht die ukrainische Armee über das geisterhafte Gebiet. Und bereitet sich darauf vor, dass der Feind zurückkommt.

spiegel.title: Syrien: Damaskus und Moskau einigen sich auf Nutzung russischer Stützpunkte
spiegel.description: Syrien und Russland haben sich auf eine künftige Nutzung der verbliebenen russischen Stützpunkte verständigt. Russlands Militär könnte somit weiter in dem Land präsent bleiben.

spiegel.title: Tour de France Femmes: Demi Vollering gewinnt erneut – Niedermaier bestes Nachwuchstalent
spiegel.description: Bereits 2023 war es ihr gelungen, nun siegt sie erneut: Die Niederländerin Demi Vollering holt sich Platz eins der Tour de France der Frauen. Antonia Niedermaier gewann das Trikot als beste Nachwuchsfahrerin.

spiegel.title: Schleswig-Holstein: Pilot stirbt bei Absturz von Kleinflugzeug
spiegel.description: Westlich von Hamburg ist ein Flugzeug in ein Feld gestürzt. Der einzige Insasse überlebte den Absturz nicht. Experten für die Untersuchung von Flugunfällen sind auf dem Weg zur Unglücksstelle.

spiegel.title: Pfadfinder-Bundeslager: Das Versprechen von Frieden und Freundschaft
spiegel.description: Auf einem staubigen Feld in Hessen errichten 6000 Pfadfinder Zelte, Küchen und Werkstätten. Und schaffen eine Gegenwelt aus Gemeinschaft und Verantwortung.

spiegel.title: Drohnen in Deutschland: Wie gut das Land gegen Attacken aus der Luft gerüstet ist
spiegel.description: Nach der Sprengstoffdrohne am Leipziger Flughafen wurde am Bundeswehrstandort Mechernich erneut eine Drohne gesichtet. Wie geht die deutsche Politik mit dem Problem um – und welche Abwehrmaßnahmen gibt es bisher?

spiegel.title: Berlin: Hunderte Lehrer fallen wegen Krankheit dauerhaft aus
spiegel.description: Mehr als 200 verbeamtete Lehrer in Berlin sind seit mindestens einem Jahr krankgeschrieben, hinzu kommen rund 150 angestellte Lehrkräfte. Die meisten von ihnen arbeiten an Grundschulen.

spiegel.title: Yuval Noah Harari über Künstliche Intelligenz: »Wie berechnet man die Kosten der Auslöschung?«
spiegel.description: Der israelische Historiker Yuval Noah Harari sagt, die Menschheit sollte sich mehr vor US-Techunternehmen fürchten als vor Killerrobotern. Und wenn Europa keine eigene KI entwickele, werde es zum Vasall der USA.

spiegel.title: Bremen: Mordkommission ermittelt nach tödlichem Angriff auf einen Fußgänger
spiegel.description: Ein Mann starb am Samstagnachmittag in der Bremer Neustadt, nachdem ein Autofahrer ihn ins Gesicht geschlagen hatte. Nun sucht die Polizei nach Zeugen. Möglicherweise handelte es sich um eine zufällige Begegnung.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Nackte Fahrraddemonstration – »Wie Schwimmen in der Luft«
spiegel.description: Rund 500 Menschen sind nackt durch Berlin geradelt. Sie wollen für die schrumpfende FKK-Bewegung werben – unter anderem.

letemps.description:
La grande fête jurassienne du cheval a été marquée dimanche par la première participation de Berne en tant qu’hôte d’honneur. Ce rapprochement avec le Jura, après des années de tensions, ne fait pas oublier les difficultés que doivent affronter les éleveurs de franches-montagnes

letemps.description:

observador.description: "Embora tenha faltado dimensão competitiva", Gabriel Alves deixa elogios ao comportamento do Alverca no Dragão. Mesmo apesar da vitória, o Porto foi-lhe "geométrico" e faltou-lhe "nota artística".

observador.title: As mães modernas
observador.description: Não entendo que as mães ou sejam mães-galinha ou mães-helicóptero; gosto que sejam “só” mães! Com direito ao sexto sentido, aos erros e aos “exageros”. Mas mágicas, espontâneas e livres.

observador.title: FC Porto estende a festa e volta a ser igual a si próprio
observador.description: O FC Porto bateu este domingo o Alverca (2-0). Os dragões marcaram os golos do triunfo na primeira parte, ambos através de penálti. André Silva apontou o primeiro (9') e Gabri fechou a contagem (44').

observador.title: Bombeiros pedem a PR para ajudar na reforma do setor
observador.description: O presidente da Liga dos Bombeiros Portugueses pediu ao Presidente da República para usar a sua "magistratura de influência" para "acelerar a discussão pública" sobre a reforma estrutural do setor.

observador.title: Fogos. do Presidente são alerta para se pensar e corrigir
observador.description: As chamadas de atenção e os reparos do Presidente da República são sempre vistos como uma forma de alerta e para se pensar e poder corrigir aquilo que há a corrigir, diz Luís Neves.

observador.title: "Eu, Giorgia". A autobiografia de Meloni antes do poder
observador.description: Antes de ser PM, Meloni elogiava Trump, mas queria aproximação à Rússia. E criticava o "eixo franco-alemão" da UE, com quem veio a entender-se. O Observador publica alguns excertos de "Eu, Giorgia".

observador.title: Prestianni também acerta no poste (1-0, 23')
observador.description: A estreia do Benfica no Campeonato, no jogo que marca o regresso do Ac. Viseu, acontece à porta fechada, por castigo da APCVD. Marco Silva repete onze que goleou Hearts. Siga aqui em direto.

observador.title: Mulher ferida com gravidade em colisão aquática no Alqueva
observador.description: Uma mulher ficou hoje gravemente ferida e foi helitransportada para um hospital de Lisboa após uma colisão aquática no Alqueva, perto da Praia do Lago, no concelho de Moura.

observador.title: Madeira e Porto Santo sob aviso amarelo devido a calor
observador.description: As costas norte e sul da Madeira e o Porto Santo estão sob aviso amarelo devido ao tempo quente até quarta-feira, indicou o Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera (IPMA).

observador.title: As portas fecharam-se, mas a Luz acendeu-se junto ao Rei
observador.description: Com a Luz fechada, os adeptos reuniram-se na fan zone, onde não faltou comida, ecrãs e até bandeiras, numa receção apoteótica junto à estátua de Eusébio. Medida gerou controvérsia nos últimos dias.

observador.title: 19h. Volta Portugal. Alexis Guérin é o novo camisola amarela
observador.description: A quarta etapa ligou Figueiró dos Vinhos à Covilhã, com a chegada ao alto, na Torre. Alexis Guérin foi o primeiro a cortar a meta, após mais de 150 kms na estrada. Ainda, a atualidade internacional.

observador.title: Destroços de navio romano descobertos na costa da Sicília
observador.description: Um grupo de mergulhadores encontrou destroços de um navio da época romana, que se suspeita ser do século II e I A.C. Foram encontradas centenas de ânforas em bom estado.

observador.title: Associação ucraniana questiona PS sobre deputado na Rússia
observador.description: Associação dos Ucranianos em Portugal questionou o PS sobre deputado socialista que acusa de elogiar a Rússia em viagem de comboio pelo país. Partido Socialista diz que "não corresponde à realidade".

observador.title: Confrontos com a polícia no Uíge fazem 31 feridos, diz UNITA
observador.description: Pelo menos 31 pessoas ficaram feridas, dez com gravidade, na sequência da intervenção da polícia junto à sede da UNITA no Uíge, no sábado, disse secretário-geral da JURA, organização juvenil da Unita.

observador.title: Governo reforça compensações por ataques de lobo ibérico
observador.description: O regime de compensações aos produtores agropecuários cujos rebanhos sejam atacados pelo lobo ibérico foi revisto para reforçar as indemnizações e os critérios de elegibilidade.

observador.title: 17h. Liga Portugal. FC Porto entra em campo frente a Alverca
observador.description: E depois é a vez do Benfica entrar em campo. Ainda, o Hamas pede aos Estados Unidos que intervenham perante Israel .

observador.title: Prisão domiciliária para suspeito de três fogos
observador.description: A PJ deteve um homem fortemente indiciado por três crimes de incêndio florestal, ocorridos entre 4 de julho e 1 de agosto, em Vila Nova de Poiares, e o tribunal determinou prisão domiciliária.

observador.title: Serra da Estrela. Revitalização é promessa por cumprir
observador.description: O Presidente da República lembrou que revitalização do Parque Natural da Serra da Estrela é uma promessa que "se arrasta há demasiado tempo", desde o incêndio de 2022 que "durou mais de duas semanas".

nzz.title: Demi Vollering gewinnt die Tour de France zum zweiten Mal – Marlen Reusser verliert am letzten Tag ihren Podestplatz
nzz.description: Eine packende fünfte Ausgabe der Tour de France Femmes geht am Sonntag mit einem Triumph der Nummer 1 der Welt zu Ende. Die Niederländerin gewinnt in Nizza solo mit ihrem dritten Etappensieg.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Hunderte fliehen vor Waldbrand im Südwesten Spaniens
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

nzz.title: Super League: Der FC Thun verliert in Basel 2:4 und hilft dem Trainer Stephan Lichtsteiner im Ringen um Wohlwollen
nzz.description: Der Meister aus dem Berner Oberland hat den Kopf derzeit anderswo und erhält in zwei Spielen gegen YB und Basel zehn Gegentore. Das wirft Fragen auf, wird aber zur willkommenen Einladung für die Stabilität suchende Konkurrenz.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Teheran tauscht obersten Sicherheitsberater aus
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Mehrere Verletzte durch Schüsse in dänischer Stadt
nzz.description: Am Sonntagnachmittag sind Schüsse in einer Wohngegend der dänischen Kleinstadt Holbæk gefallen. Die Polizei ist mit vielen Kräften vor Ort und fahndet nach den flüchtigen Tätern.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Mehrere Tote bei russischen Angriffen +++ Bis zu 50 000 nordkoreanische Soldaten kommen laut Selenski nach Russland
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: Iran will die Strasse von Hormuz erst öffnen, wenn die USA ihre Truppen abziehen und die Sanktionen aufheben
nzz.description: Washington wird die harten Bedingungen Teherans kaum akzeptieren können. Derweil attackieren die Huthi eine Raffinerie in Saudiarabien – ein schnelles Kriegsende ist unwahrscheinlich.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Bilder zum 79. Locarno Film Festival
nzz.description: Bis zum 15. August steht Locarno ganz im Zeichen des Films. Auf der Piazza Grande geben sich Stars wie Monica Bellucci, Isabella Rossellini und Olivia Wilde die Ehre.

nzz.title: Spanien führt Grenzkontrollen für Reisende aus Italien ein
nzz.description: Spanien und Italien kontrollieren Einreisende aus den jeweiligen Ländern gegenseitig. Die Politik der diplomatischen Nadelstiche geht zurück auf die Migrationskrise in Ceuta.

nzz.title: In Polen häufen sich Beleidigungen und gewaltsame Übergriffe gegen Ukrainer
nzz.description: Im Internet werden Ressentiments gegen angeblich undankbare ukrainische Kriegsflüchtlinge geschürt. Auch der Streit um die Massaker im Zweiten Weltkrieg vergiftet die Atmosphäre. Aber weiterhin gibt es Polen, die sich schützend vor die Ukrainer stellen.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Europa in der Gluthitze: die Bilder des Rekordsommers
nzz.description: Der Sommer 2026 brennt sich ins kollektive Gedächtnis ein: ausgetrocknete Flüsse, brennende Wälder und Rekordtemperaturen. Auch in den kommenden Tagen bleibt uns das extreme Wetter erhalten.

Todd Blanche als neuer US-Justizminister bestätigt

nzz.title: Laut seinem Sohn Hunter hat sich der Krebs bei Joe Biden ausgebreitet und verursacht grosse Schmerzen
nzz.description: Der ehemalige amerikanische Präsident Joe Biden leidet an einer besonders aggressiven Form von Prostatakrebs. Sein Sohn Hunter hat den kräftezehrenden Kampf gegen die Krankheit geschildert und sich gewünscht, sein Vater würde sich öfter mal beschweren.

nzz.title: Elena Fischers neuer Roman: «Dies ist nicht mein Leben. Tut mir leid.»
nzz.description: Als sich Bauer Joseph schon den Lauf des Gewehres in den Mund gesteckt hat, klingelt es an der Tür. So beginnt «Wirf einen Schatten», der feinsinnige neue Roman von Elena Fischer.

elpais.title: “Ceuta no se vende”: la ciudad se echa a la calle tras diez días de tensión

elpais.description: Con destinos del interior con lleno total desde hace más de un año y miles de personas que tomarán una decisión a última hora, España vivirá este 12 de agosto un fenómeno astronómico único que supondrá un desafío para las autoridades

elpais.title: Arcos de las Salinas, el pueblo turolense que teme desbordarse de turistas por el eclipse: “Vamos a morir de éxito”
elpais.description: El municipio de 80 habitantes está a las faldas del cerro que alberga el mayor centro de divulgación astronómica de Europa, pero no cuenta con plazas hoteleras ni servicios

elpais.title: Fergie Chambers, el activista millonario detenido en Ibiza: “Soy un defensor de los derechos humanos”
elpais.description: Los abogados del estadounidense, encabezados por Baltasar Garzón, denuncian una “persecución política” por parte de Trump por su apoyo a Palestina. El Gobierno tendrá que decidir si lo extradita

elpais.title: Charlotte Gainsbourg: “Me siento bastante cómoda con la idea de ser una impostora”
elpais.description: Después de la muerte de Serge Gainsbourg, venerado como un rey en un país republicano, su casa en París se convirtió en un sitio de peregrinaciones de millones de fans. elpais.title: La nueva era de las redes sociales y los artistas: ya no te cuentan su vida como antes
elpais.description: Los perfiles de Instagram se profesionalizan y los contenidos más personales se limitan ante los riesgos que las estrellas de la cultura perciben al compartir sus reflexiones más personales

elpais.title: Carlos Senghor Diatta no quiere ser futbolista
elpais.description: El activista Moha Gerehou observa más hostilidad en los espacios compartidos. Hay pocos niños y molestan

elpais.title: De San Sebastián a Barcelona: por qué empieza a ser habitual (y práctico) pasear con sombrillas de mano
elpais.description: Más olas de calor, ciudades poco preparadas para afrontarlo y mucha  necesidad de sombra. El paraguas para el sol ha dejado de ser un gesto de turistas asiáticos para convertirse en un objeto cotidiano en Europa

elpais.title: Diez recetas de aperitivos para disfrutar el resto del verano
elpais.description: Con hortalizas de temporada, con pescado o con huevos puedes hacer todas estas recetas para abrir el apetito o para preparar una comida entera

elpais.title: ¿Por qué se ríen de ‘La odisea’ de Christopher Nolan?
elpais.description: Estamos siendo asaltados por un gran caballo de Troya que alcanza pueblos y países pacíficos sin que podamos hacer nada

nyt.title: Iran, Holding Firm to Hormuz, Pushes for Return to June MOU
nyt.description: The Strait of Hormuz is Iran’s best leverage to get Washington to release Iran’s frozen assets, lift economic sanctions and end its naval blockade.

nyt.title: Inside the War on Hezbollah’s Finances
nyt.description: Israel and the United States aren’t just targeting the Lebanese militant group’s weapons. They’re going after its money.

nyt.title: Iran Taps Longtime I.R.G.C. Commander Mohsen Rezaei to Top Security Post
nyt.description: The appointment of Mohsen Rezaei as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council suggests that Iran’s old guard is consolidating power.

nyt.title: Israel Rejects Trump’s 15-Point Plan to Disarm Hamas
nyt.description: President Trump’s Board of Peace announced an agreement last month that aimed at Hamas’s giving up its weapons alongside an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza.

nyt.title: Trump Crypto Took $100 Million From a Businessman With Red Flags
nyt.description: The curious case of Guren “Bobby” Zhou shows the ease with which investors with shady backgrounds and unknown motivations can funnel money to the president.

nyt.title: The Lonely Crew at the Kennedy Center Will Miss Its…Mice

nyt.title: Obama and Abdul El-Sayed Spoke to Discuss Unity After Michigan Senate Primary
nyt.description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s call with the former president comes as he tries to win over wary Democrats in Michigan’s high-stakes Senate race.

nyt.title: Michigan Senate Candidate, a Former Trump Critic, Shifts Toward Election Skepticism
nyt.description: Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee, has suggested that further scrutiny of the 2020 election was warranted and that voting irregularities sank his first Senate bid two years ago.

nyt.title: Ocasio-Cortez Says She Is Freezing Her Eggs and Still Mulling a Presidential Run
nyt.description: In a TV interview, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez distanced herself from positions like “defund the police” and indicated she hasn’t ruled out a presidential or Senate run.

nyt.title: A Democrat Sounds the Alarm on Christian Nationalism in Congress
nyt.description: Representative Jared Huffman of California, the only self-declared “humanist” in Congress, writes in a new book that the separation of church and state is in grave danger.

nyt.title: How a Drone ‘Hellscape’ Might Stop a Chinese Invasion of Taiwan
nyt.description: Inspired by Ukraine’s battlefield gains, Taiwan is betting on drones to deter a potential Chinese invasion.

nyt.title: The ‘Furthur’ Bus’s Long, Strange Trip, and Why It’s Returning to San Francisco
nyt.description: Ken Kesey’s psychedelic bus, immortalized in “The Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test,” is preparing for one more run. And to its owners, America sure could use it.

nyt.title: Anthony Scaramucci, Podcast Star, Explains U.S. Politics to the World
nyt.description: He spent 11 days in the Trump White House nine years ago. Now he has a hit podcast, helping the British public, among others, understand what’s going on.

nyt.title: Please Judge the Books I’m Reading

npr.title: Netanyahu rejects Trump's Gaza Peace Plan, demands Hamas disarm first
npr.description: Netanyahu's comments come just over a week after President Trump said his Board of Peace had reached a "historic" agreement with Hamas to give up its weapons.

npr.title: In Munich, it's never too early for a breakfast beer with sausage and pretzels
npr.description: Bavarians traditionally wash down a breakfast of boiled veal sausage, sweet mustard and a giant pretzel with beer — all before the church bells ring at midday.

npr.title: This rising painter reimagines Renaissance art in a cocoa plantation in Cameroon
npr.description: A new gallery show in London features the paintings of Marc Padeu, playing with themes from Renaissance art and bringing them to his homeland of Cameroon.

npr.title: Tanker sailors still face danger in the Strait of Hormuz
npr.description: An agreement over the Strait of Hormuz is still far away. Tim Wilkins, who works for a tanker industry group, says the ships stuck around the waterway are in limbo, and transiting is still dangerous.

npr.title: Switzerland is a neutral nation but has more nuclear bunkers than any country in the world
npr.description: Instead of scrapping its network of bomb shelters after the Cold War, Switzerland kept building them. The country has more than 370,000 nuclear bomb shelters. Some are now used to house migrants.

proj-syn.title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration
proj-syn.description: When tens of thousands of people recently entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco, European leaders lapsed into recriminations, reigniting the debate on migration. But the bigger challenge is to address a long-simmering territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.

proj-syn.title: The Rising Price of a Cheap Renminbi
proj-syn.description: Renminbi appreciation would not, on its own, rebalance China’s economy and eliminate its massive surpluses. But by increasing households’ purchasing power over imports and compressing tradable-sector margins, it would raise the cost of avoiding reform.

proj-syn.title: Who Should Build the Low-Carbon Economy?
proj-syn.description: Since the first Industrial Revolution, goods and technologies have reached the farthest corners of the world, but the ability to design, build, market, and extract value from them has remained highly concentrated. Unless humanity can break this pattern, a sufficient response to climate change will remain out of reach.

proj-syn.title: Will Iceland Rejoin the EU Path?
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s volatile and unpredictable security policies, particularly his desire to control Greenland, have put Iceland in a vulnerable position. This uncomfortable reality will likely be front of mind as voters decide whether to reopen membership negotiations with the European Union.

proj-syn.title: Democracy, Autocracy, or Something Else?
proj-syn.description: Contrary to conventional wisdom, the world is neither converging on liberal democracy nor being swept by an authoritarian tide. The decisive political struggles of the 21st century will be won or lost through the unglamorous work of strengthening democratic accountability and building effective institutions.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s New Right-Wing Government Faces an Uphill Battle
proj-syn.description: Colombian President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella inherits an economy constrained by weak investment and a severe fiscal crisis. His ability to restore fiscal stability without sacrificing the social gains of recent decades will determine whether the country’s rightward shift proves lasting or short-lived.

proj-syn.title: Can Progressives Deliver Economic Growth?
proj-syn.description: At a time of historic inequality and inadequate public investment, the kind of redistributive policies promoted by politicians on the left are badly needed. But given that no jurisdiction can tax and regulate its way to affordability, a growth-enhancing agenda that generates good jobs and productive capacity is also vital.

proj-syn.title: Fauci’s Modern Pillory
proj-syn.description: MAGA Republicans’ decision to drag Anthony Fauci before a Senate hearing was less about their hatred of science and more about their disdain for the scientists who guide lawmakers in their decision-making. They couldn’t wait to pillory him, and by association any public-facing expert, in front of the cameras.

proj-syn.title: Cheaper Mortgages Won’t Solve the US Housing Crisis
proj-syn.description: For decades, federal housing policy has favored cheaper financing over expanding the housing supply, despite evidence that expanding mortgage credit increases borrowing and house prices. The bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act marks an important shift by emphasizing measures that make it easier to build more homes.

proj-syn.title: The Right Way to Regulate AI
proj-syn.description: Governments tend to treat AI as a national-security challenge while devoting far less attention to its effects on education, health, labor markets, and the judiciary. Addressing AI’s societal risks requires institutions designed to recognize and respond to emerging threats before they become systemic failures.

proj-syn.title: Global Tax Reform Is the Key to a Fair AI Economy
proj-syn.description: The rise of AI has highlighted how the global tax system is ill-suited to capture the profits derived from such technology. While creating an equitable AI economy ultimately requires a durable and robust multilateral tax framework, digital-service taxes can serve as an important stepping stone to that outcome.

proj-syn.title: Aid’s Next Chapter
proj-syn.description: Wars, epidemics, displacement, and geopolitical competition will ensure that rich countries continue to spend money abroad, whether for humanitarian reasons or in pursuit of their own interests. The only question is what sort of aid system will emerge from the current retrenchment.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Won’t Last Unless It Benefits Ordinary Iranians
proj-syn.description: A sustainable peace agreement between the United States and Iran will require more than military deterrence. Without financial sanctions relief that fuels job creation and generates real economic opportunities for ordinary Iranians, it will likely suffer the same fate as the 2015 nuclear deal.

proj-syn.title: Why Wealth Taxes Always Fail
proj-syn.description: A clear-eyed view of past experience shows that where wealth taxes have been tried, they have usually been abandoned—and for good reason. As policymakers in California, New York, France, and elsewhere revisit this old idea, they should heed the lessons of this history.

proj-syn.title: A New Paradigm for Global Health Financing
proj-syn.description: As aid flows decline, more countries are articulating a new vision in which health financing would build on national resources, answer to domestic priorities, and remain accountable to their own citizens. Such a change is long overdue, and it can be achieved by pursuing reforms in three areas.

proj-syn.title: The Triumph of India’s Cockroaches
proj-syn.description: The concessions secured by the "cockroach movement" amount to more than a triumph for prospective medical students or a brief political headache for the country's ruling party. They prove that even after years of centralization and institutional erosion, power remains with the people.

proj-syn.title: Zombie Monetarism
proj-syn.description: Three prominent economists, including a former Federal Reserve governor and adviser to US President Donald Trump, have just endorsed “soft monetarism” as a way to guide the Fed's approach to inflation. But the "quantity theory" of money failed for good reasons, and those reasons have not changed.

To avert a Chinese invasion, Taiwan must ensure that other democracies cannot function without it by providing them with more than just semiconductors.

crunchbase.description: We analyzed a dataset of repeat founders who have gone through Y Combinator’s cohorts and found some very interesting insights. The dataset, shared with us directly from YC, consisted of 454 repeat founders through the program as well as 935 founder-company records spanning 2005 through 2026. We spoke to a couple of them about their experiences.

crunchbase.title: Your AI Strategy May Be Destroying Your Exit Value
crunchbase.description: While integrating AI into a startup's product strategy is often viewed as a way to enhance valuation, it can inadvertently reduce exit value, argues tech strategic adviser Itay Sagie. In this guest commentary he shares three ways your AI strategy can provide a positive impact on valuation when it becomes time for an exit.

crunchbase.title: A Record 14 Billion-Dollar Rounds In July Pushed Venture’s Historic Run Higher

crunchbase.title: Why The Product Manager To CEO Pipeline Is The Underrated Crash Course For Leadership In Tech
crunchbase.description: Traditional research on CEO career paths tends to focus on titles such as COO, CFO and divisional president. But the skills developed in product management may be just as relevant, argues Paysend CEO Ben Chisell. In this guest column, he makes the case that aspiring leaders should focus less on collecting prestigious titles and more on taking ownership of measurable business outcomes.

crunchbase.title: ‘A Rare Land-Grab Moment’: Menlo Ventures’ Matt Murphy On The Next Wave of AI And Putting $3B In New Capital To Work
crunchbase.description: We speak with Menlo Ventures' Matt Murphy about why AI is pushing the firm toward larger deals, what it has learned from its Anthropic relationship, and where he sees the next big opportunities.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Safe Superintelligence And Commonwealth Fusion Lead With Billion-Dollar Deals
crunchbase.description: Another week, another bevy of big rounds. The largest round was a reported $5 billion Nvidia-backed financing for foundational AI unicorn Safe Superintelligence, followed by a $1 billion investment in Commonwealth Fusion Systems.
